newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: China jails N. Korean for abducting Seoul pastor.
newsitem.headline: China jails N. Korean for abducting Seoul pastor.

text.p: South Korea said on Monday that Chinese authorities had convicted a North Korean of abducting a Seoul pastor travelling in China last year.

A South Korean foreign ministry statement said China notified Seoul last Friday that its judiciary authorities had sentenced Li Gyong-chun to two years in prison on charges of kidnapping the Reverend Ahn Seung-un of Seoul's Full Gospel Church and taking him to the North.

Li, who was arrested in China in July last year shortly after Ahn was discovered to be in the North, has given up appealing against the sentence and will be deported after serving the jail term, the statement said.

"Now that it has been confirmed that Ahn Seung-un, against his own free will, was kidnapped by a North Korean in Chinese territory, we ask the Chinese government to take all necessary steps and make diplomatic efforts for Ahn's return," it said.
The Seoul unification ministry's demanded that the North immediately return the pastor.

"North Korean authorities should immediately repatriate Mr Ahn Seung-un, punish those involved and apologise to our government and people for the kidnapping," said spokesman Kim Kyung-woong in a statement.
The reclusive Stalinist North has said Ahn, who was sent to an ethnic Korean area of northeastern China in May 1991 for missionary work, had defected.

At the time, Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency quoted Ahn as saying he was sent to the Yanbian area of China by the South's security agency to "allure cadres of the northern half of Korea".
South Korea has said that the North was believed to have taken Ahn against his will and has called for his repatriation.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after a 1950-53 conflict that ended only with a truce. The two sides have never agreed on a peace pact.
